questions.stem: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee recently raised the policy repo rate, adjusting other rates in the liquidity adjustment facility corridor. Consider the following statements regarding RBI's rate instruments and the Monetary Policy Committee. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The policy repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against the collateral of government securities.
The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) requires banks to pledge government securities as collateral when depositing surplus funds with RBI.
The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) allows banks to borrow overnight funds from RBI at a rate higher than the repo rate, acting as a penal-rate liquidity window.
The Monetary Policy Committee consists of six members, three from the RBI and three experts appointed by the Central Government.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is false: the SDF, introduced in April 2022 to replace the fixed-rate reverse repo, is a collateral-free facility to absorb excess liquidity — that collateral-free feature is precisely why it was introduced. Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct: repo lending is against G-secs, MSF sits above repo as a penal overnight window, and the MPC under the RBI Act, 1934 has three RBI members and three government-appointed experts.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: What is the impact of 25 basis points repo rate hike on borrowers? | Explained
questions.pyqLink: Tests the LAF rate corridor (repo/SDF/MSF/Bank Rate) and MPC composition under the RBI Act, 1934 — cf. UPSC 2021 question on RBI's expansionist monetary policy tools.

questions.stem: The 57th GST Council meeting concluded with several administrative decisions. Consider the following statements about the GST Council. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A and is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
A decision of the GST Council requires a majority of not less than two-thirds of the weighted votes of members present and voting.
In the GST Council, the Central Government has one-third of the total votes cast, and all State Governments together have two-thirds of the votes cast.
Recommendations of the GST Council are binding on both Parliament and State Legislatures in all matters of indirect taxation.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, matching Article 279A's composition and voting-weight scheme. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 279A(9) requires a three-fourths majority of weighted votes, not two-thirds. Statement 4 is wrong: in Mohit Minerals v. Union of India (2022), the Supreme Court held GST Council recommendations are only persuasive/recommendatory, not binding on Parliament or State Legislatures.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: GST Council Meeting Oct 2026: List of decisions taken - arrest, prosecution, general penalty and more
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 279A voting structure and the Mohit Minerals ruling on cooperative federalism — cf. UPSC 2021 Cabinet Secretariat statement-based question.

questions.stem: The Finance Ministry has directed bankers' committees to report Scheduled Caste beneficiary data to assist the National Commission for Scheduled Castes in its constitutional functions. With reference to the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: NCSC is a constitutional body functioning under Article 338, while the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes functions under the separately inserted Article 338A.
A person must have previously held a constitutional post for at least ten years to be eligible for appointment as Chairperson of the NCSC.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the combined SC/ST Commission, giving NCSC Article 338 and creating Article 338A for NCST. Statement 2 is fabricated — there is no such ten-year prior-constitutional-post eligibility criterion for NCSC Chairperson appointment.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Why have SLBCs/UTLBCs been asked to report SC beneficiary data for key government schemes for jobs and entrepreneurship? | Explained

questions.stem: The GST Council's recent reforms have renewed attention on the constitutional and economic design of India's Goods and Services Tax. Consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Integrated GST (IGST) levied on inter-State supplies is collected and retained solely by the Central Government, with no portion devolved to the destination State.
Article 246A, inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, confers concurrent power on Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws on goods and services tax.
GST is a destination-based consumption tax, under which tax revenue accrues to the State where goods or services are finally consumed rather than produced.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — Article 246A creates concurrent taxing power, and GST's destination principle sends revenue to the consuming State. Statement 1 is wrong: under the IGST Act, inter-State IGST collections are apportioned between the Centre and the destination State, not retained wholly by the Centre.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India's GST Revolution: How India's biggest indirect tax reform changed its economy
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 246A and the destination-based principle of GST — core static concept behind recurring GST Council news.

questions.stem: News reports suggest the rollout of a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions may be deferred to January 1. With reference to the term 'Merchant Discount Rate', which one of the following best describes it?
options: The rate of interest charged by banks on merchant cash credit accounts used for working capital.
The interchange fee paid by card-issuing banks to the Reserve Bank of India for operating the National Financial Switch.
The statutory minimum discount merchants must offer to customers paying via UPI, as mandated under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act.
The fee charged by a bank or payment service provider to a merchant for enabling digital payment transactions, usually computed as a percentage of the transaction value.
questions.explanation: MDR is the charge levied on a merchant by banks/payment service providers for processing digital payment transactions, typically as a percentage of transaction value — currently zero on UPI P2M transactions, which is why its proposed reintroduction is contentious. The other options invent unrelated concepts (cash credit interest, NFS interchange fee, a fabricated statutory discount) that do not describe MDR.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: UPI MDR rollout may be deferred beyond festive season to Jan 1; shares fall: Report
questions.pyqLink: Direct repeat of UPSC 2019 Prelims: 'Which one of the following best describes the term Merchant Discount Rate?'

questions.stem: India recently joined 14 other economies in endorsing a G20 joint ministerial statement on global manufacturing overcapacity. Consider the following two statements.
statements: Statement-I: India, along with the US, EU, Japan, Australia and ten other economies, has endorsed a joint statement addressing structural excess manufacturing capacity.
Statement-II: Structural excess capacity arises purely from free and undistorted market competition among producing countries, independent of any government policy or intervention.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct — 15 economies in all, including India, the US, EU, Japan and Australia, endorsed the statement. Statement-II is incorrect: the joint statement itself attributes structural excess capacity to government policies and interventions that distort markets, not to undistorted market competition.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: India signs pact to address global excess capacity: What is it? Who are the 15 signatories? Check joint statement
questions.pyqLink: Tests understanding of trade-distorting industrial policy and global value chain concentration, a recurring IR/Economy crossover theme since 2022 statement-reason questions began.

questions.stem: With reference to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The GST Council is constituted under Article 279A of the Constitution of India.
The Union Finance Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of the GST Council.
Recommendations of the GST Council are binding on both the Union and State legislatures.
questions.explanation: The GST Council was created by the 101st Constitutional Amendment under Article 279A, and the Union Finance Minister (Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the 57th meeting referenced in the article) is its ex-officio Chairperson, so statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in Mohit Minerals (2022), the Supreme Court held that GST Council recommendations are persuasive, arising from cooperative federalism, and not binding on Parliament or State legislatures.

questions.sourceTitle: GST Council unveils reforms to ease refund, registration and reduce litigation

questions.stem: Consider the following two statements in the context of the RBI's recent monetary policy decision:
statements: Statement-I: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee targets retail (CPI) inflation within a band of 4% with a tolerance of +/-2%.

Statement-II: Raising the policy repo rate curbs inflation driven by supply-side factors such as a deficient monsoon or rising global crude oil prices by directly increasing agricultural and fuel output.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I correctly describes India's flexible inflation targeting framework (CPI-based, 4% midpoint, +/-2% band), under which the RBI raised rates as inflation projections rose. Statement-II is incorrect: the article itself notes that when supply-side factors (deficient monsoon, oil prices) drive inflation, a rate hike has only 'second-order and largely marginal effects' and cannot raise agricultural or fuel output directly; its main value here is signalling, not supply correction.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Adequate response: on the RBI and inflation
questions.pyqLink: Tests flexible inflation targeting framework, similar to UPSC 2023 Statement-I/II pattern on monetary policy transmission

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding gold, silver and platinum imports under the GST regime:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Gold, silver and platinum imports by banks and nominated agencies currently attract a 3% Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST).
IGST on imports into India is levied by treating them as inter-State supply under the IGST Act, consistent with Article 269A of the Constitution.
The Reserve Bank of India is the sole authority empowered to notify the list of nominated agencies eligible for IGST-exempt gold imports.
The basic customs duty on gold and silver imports was raised to 15% as part of measures to curb non-essential imports.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 are directly confirmed by the article (3% IGST on these imports; customs duty hiked to 15% from 6%). Statement 2 is a correct static fact: imports are deemed inter-State supply under the IGST Act, and IGST is levied under Article 269A. Statement 3 is the near-miss error — the article shows it is the Government (Finance Ministry), not the RBI alone, that periodically notifies the list of nominated banks/agencies.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Gold, silver imports by banks, nominated agencies to attract 3% IGST
questions.pyqLink: Tests IGST on imports and Article 269A, an extension of UPSC's recurring GST institutional-mechanism questions

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the fourth global coral bleaching event and its impact on India's reefs:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The fourth global coral bleaching event occurred between 2023 and 2025.
Coral bleaching is triggered when a drop in sea surface temperature causes corals to expel their symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae).
The study found Lakshadweep recorded a higher proportion of bleached or dead coral cover than the Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park in the Andaman Islands.
The study concluded that bleaching severity across India's reefs was uniform and unrelated to local geographic factors.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the article confirms the 2023-2025 fourth global bleaching event, and that Lakshadweep (up to 37% affected) fared worse than MGMNP, Andaman (11.5%). Statement 2 is the near-miss error — bleaching is caused by a rise in sea surface temperature and heat stress, not a drop, which makes corals expel algae. Statement 4 directly contradicts the study, whose central finding is regional variation driven by local factors.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Study highlights regional variations in coral bleaching across India, calls for greater focus on local factors
questions.pyqLink: Tests coral bleaching mechanism and India's reef regions, similar to UPSC questions on Ramsar sites/ecological phenomena anchored to news

questions.stem: With reference to pneumonic plague, which one of the following best describes the disease?
options: It is a viral respiratory disease transmitted exclusively through contaminated water sources, with no natural animal reservoir.

It is the most severe clinical form of plague, caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, capable of person-to-person transmission through respiratory droplets, with the pathogen occurring naturally in some wild rodent populations.
It is a prion-based degenerative disease linked only to laboratory accidents at research institutes, with no occurrence in the wild.
It is a mosquito-borne disease caused by a flavivirus and is classified by the WHO as a vector-borne notifiable disease requiring mandatory nationwide lockdowns.
questions.explanation: Pneumonic plague is the most severe and rapidly fatal form of plague, caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis; unlike bubonic plague it can spread person-to-person via respiratory droplets, and the bacterium occurs naturally in wild rodent populations — consistent with the Irkutsk institute working on a disease that 'occurs naturally in wild animals.' The other options wrongly describe it as viral, prion-based, or mosquito-borne, none of which matches its established bacteriology.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia? What we know so far
questions.pyqLink: Tests static microbiology/epidemiology of plague, similar to UPSC 2019 question on diseases caused by bacteria vs viruses

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of Indian coral reef regions and their predominant reef type:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep is India's only true atoll reef formation, while the Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay — both surveyed in the coral bleaching study — are classic fringing reef regions, making the first three pairs correct. The fourth pair is wrong: the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (including Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park, also surveyed) predominantly have fringing and barrier reefs, not atolls.

questions.stem: With reference to the recent U.S. suspension of IT firms from a visa-linked programme, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Permanent Labour Certification Programme (PERM) is a pathway through which U.S. employers sponsor foreign workers, including H-1B visa holders, for permanent resident status (green cards).
Under its GATS schedule at the WTO, the United States has made binding commitments guaranteeing unrestricted Mode 4 movement of foreign professionals into its territory.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 matches the article: PERM is the U.S. programme used by employers to seek green cards for H-1B workers, and it is this programme from which Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL and others were suspended. Statement 2 is incorrect — Mode 4 (movement of natural persons) is the least liberalised mode under GATS, and WTO members, including the US, have made only limited, non-binding commitments, not a guarantee of market access.

questions.stem: With reference to stem-cell/bone marrow donor registries, consider the following statements. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: A stem-cell donor registry records a potential donor's Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) profile for matching with patients.
A majority of patients requiring a stem-cell transplant have a fully HLA-matched sibling donor available.
Stem-cell transplants are used as a potentially curative treatment for disorders such as thalassaemia and aplastic anaemia.
Registering as a potential stem-cell donor typically requires providing a bone marrow biopsy sample.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: HLA typing is the basis of donor-patient matching in such registries. Statement 3 is correct: transplants can cure blood cancers and disorders like thalassaemia and aplastic anaemia. Statement 2 is wrong since only about 25-30% of patients have a fully HLA-matched sibling donor, not a majority. Statement 4 is wrong because registration involves a cheek/buccal swab, not a bone marrow biopsy.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: What are stem-cell donor registries and how do they work?
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of HLA matching and stem-cell/bone marrow transplantation, similar in style to UPSC questions on biotechnology/medical science applications.

questions.stem: With reference to Administrative Tribunals in India, in the context of a State Administrative Tribunal hearing a service-matter dispute, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Administrative Tribunals to adjudicate service matters of State Government employees can be constituted only by a law made by the State Legislature.

In L. Chandra Kumar vs Union of India (1997), the Supreme Court held that the power of judicial review of High Courts under Articles 226/227 over the orders of Administrative Tribunals cannot be excluded.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct: the Supreme Court in L. Chandra Kumar (1997) held that High Courts' judicial review power under Articles 226/227 over Tribunal orders is part of the basic structure and cannot be ousted. Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 323A empowers Parliament, not the State Legislature, to establish Administrative Tribunals for service matters of Union and State employees through the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Keralam DHS appointment challenged in KAT
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 323A vs 323B and the L. Chandra Kumar judgment on judicial review of tribunals, a recurring Polity static theme.

questions.stem: With reference to India's semiconductor and electronics manufacturing ecosystem, in the context of global chipmakers launching new mobile processors for Indian smartphone brands, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The India Semiconductor Mission is implemented under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology to promote chip design, fabrication and packaging in India.
The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for large-scale electronics manufacturing provides incentives exclusively for the assembly of fully imported semiconductor chips.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the India Semiconductor Mission functions under MeitY to build domestic chip design, fabrication and packaging capacity. Statement 2 is incorrect because the PLI Scheme for large-scale electronics manufacturing incentivises domestic manufacturing of mobile phones and specified components, not merely the assembly of imported chips; semiconductor fabrication is separately supported under the India Semiconductor Mission.

questions.stem: With reference to Mysuru Dasara, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Mysuru Dasara is celebrated to commemorate the victory of Goddess Chamundeshwari over the demon Mahishasura, after whom Mysuru is believed to be named.
The Jamboo Savari procession traditionally carries the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari on a decorated elephant from the Mysuru Palace to Bannimantap.
Mysuru Dasara was first started by the Wodeyar dynasty in the twentieth century, after India's independence.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct and describe the well-established legend and ritual associated with Mysuru Dasara, including the Jamboo Savari procession ending at Bannimantap. Statement 3 is incorrect since the tradition traces back to the Vijayanagara Empire in the 16th century and was continued by the Wodeyars from 1610 onward, long before independence.

One of India's major natural harbour ports, located on the east coast between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal
Lies within the Northern Circars region of the Andhra Pradesh coastal plain
A hill station located in the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh

questions.stem: With reference to modern smartphone processors such as the recently announced Snapdragon chip integrating a custom CPU, GPU and NPU, which one of the following best describes a 'System-on-Chip (SoC)'?
options: A device that stores data temporarily and loses its content when power is switched off, used as the primary memory in smartphones
An integrated circuit that combines the central processing unit, graphics processing unit and other components such as a neural processing unit onto a single chip
A specialised chip that performs only graphics rendering and contains no cores for general-purpose computation
A manufacturing process node measured in nanometres that refers exclusively to the thickness of a smartphone's display panel
questions.explanation: A System-on-Chip integrates the CPU, GPU, NPU and other functional blocks onto a single piece of silicon, as seen in the Snapdragon processor combining Oryon CPU, Adreno GPU and Hexagon NPU. Option (a) describes RAM, option (c) describes a standalone GPU, and option (d) misapplies the 'process node' (a fabrication measure, e.g. 2nm) to display thickness, none of which define an SoC.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: IMC 2026: iQOO 16, Motorola Signature 27 and Xiaomi 18 Pro to run Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 processor
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static electronics/computer-architecture concept of System-on-Chip design, triggered by a current mobile-processor launch.
